rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: In Paradise, when a desired bird passes, the people say Subhanak Allah; an angel brings what they want, greets them, and they answer.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: أخبرت أن قوله: {دعواهم فيها سبحانك اللهم

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: After eating, the people praise God, which Ibn Jurayj identifies with the verse's final invocation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: أخبرت أن قوله: {دعواهم فيها سبحانك اللهم

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says that after eating they praise their Lord, fulfilling the final invocation of praise.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: أخبرت أن قوله: {دعواهم فيها سبحانك اللهم

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: When the people of Paradise want food, one says Subhanak Allah; ten thousand servants bring golden platters, each with a different food, and he eats from them all.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: إذا أراد أهل الجنة أن يدعوا بالطعام قال أحدهم: {سبحانك اللهم

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Sufyan says that whenever a person in Paradise wants something, he says Subhanak Allah.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري: إذا أراد أحدهم أن يدعو بشيء قال: {سبحانك اللهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir links this greeting in Paradise with other descriptions of the greetings of the saved and the angels.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية فيها شبه من قوله: {تحيتهم يوم يلقونه سلام وأعد لهم أجرا كريما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final praise shows that God is praised and worshipped forever, in the beginning and end, in worldly life and the Hereafter; He praises Himself at creation and revelation's beginnings.
rows.anchor: هذا فيه دلالة على أن الله تعالى هو المحمود أبدا، المعبود على طول المدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says the people of Paradise are inspired to glorify and praise God as naturally as they breathe.
rows.anchor: جاء في الحديث: "إن أهل الجنة يلهمون التسبيح والتحميد كما يلهمون النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their praise continues because God's blessings repeatedly multiply and increase without limit or end.
rows.anchor: وإنما يكون ذلك كذلك لما يرون من تضاعف نعم الله عليهم، فتكرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command came with repeated, unrelenting downpour, as in the account of the sky pouring water and the earth bursting with springs.
rows.anchor: إذا جاء أمر الله من الأمطار المتتابعة، والهتان الذي لا يقلع ولا يفتر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the tannur as the earth's surface: the ground became springs and water gushed from places like ovens; Ibn Kathir says this is the stronger view and the majority view.
rows.anchor: فعن ابن عباس: التنور: وجه الأرض، أي: صارت الأرض عيونا تفور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers the interpretation that the tannur means the earth's surface, rather than the less likely place-specific reports.
rows.anchor: والأول أظهر

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali interprets the tannur as the split of dawn, meaning the light and brightness of daybreak.
rows.anchor: وعن علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه: التنور: فلق الصبح، وتنوير الفجر، وهو ضياؤه وإشراقه

rows.speaker: مجاهد والشعبي
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Sha'bi locate Noah's tannur in Kufa.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد والشعبي: كان هذا التنور بالكوفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas identifies the tannur as a spring in India.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: عين بالهند

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies it as a spring in al-Jazira called the Spring of al-Warda.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة: عين بالجزيرة، يقال لها: عين الوردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the reports locating the tannur in Kufa, India, or al-Jazira unusual.
rows.anchor: وهذه أقوال غريبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah was told to take two of every pair of living creatures, male and female; one reported view also includes plants.
rows.anchor: من صنوف المخلوقات ذوات الأرواح، قيل: وغيرها من النباتات -اثنين. ذكرا وأنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the dove entered first and the donkey last; Iblis clung to the donkey's tail, weighing it down until Noah let them both board.
rows.anchor: فقيل: كان أول من أدخل من الطيور الدرة، وآخر من أدخل من الحيوانات الحمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Iblis clung to the donkey's tail and made it too heavy to rise until Noah told it to enter even with Iblis.
rows.anchor: وجعل يريد أن ينهض فيثقله إبليس وهو متعلق بذنبه، فجعل يقول له نوح: مالك؟ ويحك.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة بن عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda reports that they could not bring the lion aboard until fever was cast upon it.
rows.anchor: وذكر أبو عبيدة بن عبد الله بن مسعود أنهم لم يستطيعوا أن يحملوا معهم الأسد، حتى ألقيت عليه الحمى

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet says fever was first sent to earth to calm the livestock beside the lion; when mice spoiled provisions, the lion sneezed out a cat that drove them away.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم. عن أبيه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لما حمل نوح في السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah was to bring his household and kin, except those already condemned for disbelief, including his son Yam and his unbelieving wife.
rows.anchor: واحمل فيها أهلك، وهم أهل بيته وقرابته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers were very few despite Noah's long stay among his people, 950 years.
rows.anchor: مع طول المدة والمقام بين أظهرهم ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says eighty people boarded, including their wives.
rows.anchor: فعن ابن عباس: كانوا ثمانين نفسا

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar gives the number as seventy-two.
rows.anchor: وعن كعب الأحبار: كانوا اثنين وسبعين نفسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported view counts only ten people.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانوا عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further report counts Noah, his three sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, their four wives, and Yam's wife.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما كانوا نوح وبنوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Noah's wife boarded, but Ibn Kathir considers this doubtful and says she likely perished because she followed her people, as Lot's wife did.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل امرأة نوح كانت معهم في السفينة، وهذا فيه نظر، بل الظاهر أنها هلكت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah says the ark's movement across the water and its final anchoring both occur in God's name.
rows.anchor: أي: بسم الله يكون جريها على وجه الماء، وبسم الله يكون منتهى سيرها، وهو رسوها

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
rows.claim: Abu Raja al-Ataridi reads the two words in the form mujriha and mursiha.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء العطاردي: "بسم الله مجريها ومرسيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction links with the prayer to praise God after reaching safety and to ask for a blessed landing; Ibn Kathir accordingly recommends naming God when beginning to ride a ship or animal.
rows.anchor: ولهذا تستحب التسمية في ابتداء الأمور: عند الركوب على السفينة وعلى الدابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Abbas says protection from drowning while aboard ships comes by invoking God's name, reciting the verse about God's grasp of the earth and heavens, then Noah's formula.
rows.anchor: قال: "أمان أمتي من الغرق إذا ركبوا في السفن أن يقولوا: بسم الله الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of God's forgiveness and mercy suits the preceding destruction of unbelievers, since other verses pair His vengeance with mercy.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {إن ربي لغفور رحيم} مناسب عند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ark sailed over water covering the whole earth and rising above mountain peaks; reports give its height as fifteen cubits or eighty miles.
rows.anchor: خمسة عشر ذراعا، وقيل: بثمانين ميلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ark moved by God's permission and under His care and protection, as other verses describe the saved being carried in the ship under divine watch.
rows.anchor: وهذه السفينة على وجه الماء سائرة بإذن الله وتحت كنفه وعنايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was sent with clear signs, proofs, and decisive arguments to Pharaoh, Egypt's king over the Copts.
rows.anchor: مخبرا عن إرسال موسى، عليه السلام، بآياته وبيناته، وحججه ودلائله الباهرة القاطعة إلى فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's people followed his deviant path and method; his command offered no guidance, only ignorance, error, disbelief, and stubbornness.
rows.anchor: أي: مسلكه ومنهجه وطريقته في الغي والضلال، {وما أمر فرعون برشيد} أي: ليس فيه رشد ولا هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Pharaoh led his people in worldly life, he will lead them to Hell and its disastrous watering place on Judgment Day, receiving the greatest share of the greater punishment.
rows.anchor: كذلك هو يقدمهم يوم القيامة إلى نار جهنم، فأوردهم إياها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaders and followers share punishment, with the leaders receiving a doubled share; the followers will complain that their chiefs misled them and ask for double punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى إخبارا عن الكفرة إنهم يقولون في النار

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A hadith from Abu Hurayra says Imru al-Qays will carry the banner of the pre-Islamic poets toward the Fire.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "امرؤ القيس حامل لواء شعراء الجاهلية إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the unseen of the heavens and earth; all affairs return to Him, and every worker will receive full recompense. He commands worship and reliance because He suffices those who trust and turn to Him.
rows.anchor: وأنه إليه المرجع والمآب، وسيوفى كل عامل عمله يوم الحساب، فله الخلق والأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing about Muhammad's deniers is hidden from God: He knows their states and words, will repay them fully in both lives, and will give Muhammad and his party victory over them.
rows.anchor: ليس يخفى عليه ما عليه مكذبوك يا محمد، بل هو عليم بأحوالهم وأقوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ka'b says that the conclusion of the Torah is the conclusion of Surat Hud.
rows.anchor: قال: خاتمة "التوراة" خاتمة "هود"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge encompasses everyone, whether they conceal or voice their words; He hears all and nothing escapes Him.
rows.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن إحاطة علمه بجميع خلقه، سواء

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says a woman came to plead about her husband while Aisha was beside the house and could not hear some of their conversation; God then revealed that He had heard their exchange.
rows.anchor: وقالت عائشة، رضي الله عنها: سبحان الذي وسع سمعه الأصوات، والله لقد جاءت المجادلة تشتكي زوجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One hidden in a house at night and one walking openly in daylight are equally within God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: ومن هو مستخف بالليل} أي: مختف في قعر بيته في ظلام الليل، {وسارب بالنهار} أي: ظاهر ماش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir explains the mu'aqqibat as guarding angels who alternate by night and day: two record deeds and two guard the person, leaving four angels with him in each period.
rows.anchor: أي: للعبد ملائكة يتعاقبون عليه، حرس بالليل وحرس بالنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound hadith says night and day angels alternate, meet at dawn and afternoon prayer, and report that they left the servants praying as they found them praying.
rows.anchor: يتعاقبون فيكم ملائكة بالليل وملائكة بالنهار، ويجتمعون في صلاة الصبح وصلاة العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another hadith says angels remain with people except during relieving themselves and intercourse, so they should be treated with modesty and respect.
rows.anchor: إن معكم من لا يفارقكم إلا عند الخلاء وعند الجماع، فاستحيوهم وأكرموهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ali ibn Abi Talha, identifies the mu'aqqibat as angels appointed by God.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {له معقبات من بين يديه ومن خلفه يحفظونه من أمر الله} والمعقبات من أمر الله، وهي الملائكة

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ikrima transmits Ibn Abbas's view that angels guard a person in front and behind, then leave when God's decree arrives.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة، عن ابن عباس: {يحفظونه من أمر الله} قال: ملائكة يحفظونه من بين يديه ومن خلفه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says each person has an angel guarding him while asleep or awake from jinn, humans, and vermin, except what God permits to reach him.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ما من عبد إلا له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report through Sufyan, Habib ibn Abi Thabit, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr says Ibn Abbas compared the attendants to a worldly king's layered guard.
rows.anchor: وقال الثوري عن حبيب بن أبي ثابت، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: {له معقبات من بين يديه ومن خلفه}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Awfi transmits Ibn Abbas's interpretation that a ruler is a partisan of Satan with guards around him.
rows.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس: {له معقبات من بين يديه ومن خلفه}

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima also interprets the attendants as rulers' escorts, preceding and following them.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة في تفسيرها: هؤلاء الأمراء: المواكب من بين يديه ومن خلفه

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the attendants as a ruler guarded against God's command, meaning the people of shirk.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: {له معقبات من بين يديه ومن خلفه يحفظونه من أمر الله} قال: هو السلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, and al-Dahhak mean that angels guarding people resemble the guards surrounding kings and rulers.
rows.anchor: يشبه حرس هؤلاء لملوكهم وأمرائهم.

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A strange report says each person has ten angels: recorders on the right and left, guards in front and behind, an angel at the forehead, two at the lips, one at the mouth, and two at the eyes; night angels replace day angels, making twenty, with Iblis and his offspring nearby.
rows.anchor: عن كنانة العدوي قال: دخل عثمان بن عفان على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم. فقال: يا رسول الله، أخبرني عن العبد، كم معه من ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls Ibn Jarir's preceding report extremely strange.
rows.anchor: وقد روى الإمام أبو جعفر ابن جرير هاهنا حديثا غريبا جدا

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet says everyone has a companion from the jinn and one from the angels; God aided him over his jinn companion, who therefore commands only good.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما منكم من أحد إلا وقد وكل به قرينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that Muslim alone transmits the immediately preceding report about each person's jinn and angel companion.
rows.anchor: انفرد بإخراجه مسلم (5) . وقوله: {يحفظونه من أمر الله}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas's interpretation that angels guard a person by God's command is transmitted by Ali ibn Abi Talha and others, and is also held by Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i.
rows.anchor: قيل: المراد حفظهم له من أمر الله. رواه علي بن أبي طلحة، وغيره، عن ابن عباس. وإليه ذهب مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reports a variant reading, with bi-amr Allah, by God's command, in place of min amr Allah.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: {يحفظونه من أمر الله} قال: وفي بعض القراءات:

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka'b says that without angels assigned to protect people at meals, drink, and private moments, devils would snatch them away.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: لو تجلى لابن آدم كل سهل وحزن، لرأى كل شيء من ذلك شياطين

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Abu Umama says every person has an angel warding off harm until he is handed over to what has been decreed for him.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو أمامة (7) ما من آدمي إلا ومعه ملك يذود عنه

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز
rows.claim: Abu Majliz recounts that when warned of attackers, Ali said each person has two angels guarding what is not decreed; once fate comes, they release him, and the appointed term is a strong shield.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مجلز: جاء رجل من مراد إلى علي، رضي الله عنه، وهو يصلي، فقال: احترس، فإن ناسا من مراد يريدون قتلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view reads the phrase as protection by God's command, consistent with the Prophet's answer that protective incantations are themselves part of God's decree.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: {يحفظونه من أمر الله} بأمر الله، كما جاء في الحديث أنهم قالوا: يا رسول الله، أرأيت رقى نسترقي بها

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim reports that God told an Israelite prophet that when a community changes from obedience to disobedience, God changes its favored condition into what it dislikes; the verse confirms this principle.
rows.anchor: حدثنا حفص بن غياث، عن أشعث، عن جهم، عن إبراهيم قال: أوحى الله إلى نبي من أنبياء بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A report from the Lord, narrated by Ali, says when a town or family turns from disobedience to obedience, God changes their punishment into mercy and what they dislike into what they love.
rows.anchor: قال: كنت إذا سكت عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ابتدأني، وإذا سألته عن الخبر أنبأني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the preceding report strange and says its chain includes someone he does not know.
rows.anchor: وهذا غريب، وفي إسناده من لا أعرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God sent Muhammad to this community to recite His revelation, He sent messengers to earlier unbelieving nations; their rejection offers Muhammad a precedent and warns his people that punishment may overtake them.
rows.anchor: وكما أرسلناك يا محمد في هذه الأمة: {لتتلو عليهم الذي أوحينا إليك}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers endured denial and harm until God's help came, and the final outcome was theirs and their followers' in both worldly life and the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: فصبروا على ما كذبوا وأوذوا حتى أتاهم نصرنا ولا مبدل لكلمات الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the people took offense at calling God al-Rahman and al-Rahim; at Hudaybiyyah they refused to write the basmala formula and said they did not know those names, a story found in Bukhari.
rows.anchor: قاله قتادة، والحديث في صحيح البخاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to call God Allah or al-Rahman confirms that both are His beautiful names.
rows.anchor: وقد قال الله تعالى: {قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A hadith from Ibn Umar says the names most beloved to God are Abdullah and Abdurrahman.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن أحب الأسماء إلى الله عبد الله وعبد الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad affirms that the one his opponents reject is his Lord, the sole God, and that he believes in His lordship and divinity.
rows.anchor: هذا الذي تكفرون به أنا مؤمن به، معترف مقر له بالربوبية والإلهية، هو ربي لا إله إلا هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad relies on God in all his affairs and returns and repents to Him, since no one else deserves this.
rows.anchor: عليه توكلت} أي: في جميع أموري، {وإليه متاب} أي: إليه أرجع وأنيب
